explain.say: In July 1853 Commodore Matthew Perry of the US Navy steamed into Edo Bay with black-hulled warships and demanded that Japan open its ports. Japan had kept most foreigners out for two centuries. Just fifty years later Japan defeated Russia in war. Look at the timeline. How did it change so fast?

explain.say: Now the map. In 1868 young samurai from the Satsuma and Chōshū domains overthrew the Tokugawa shogun, the military ruler, and restored power, in name, to the teenage Emperor Meiji. The imperial court moved from Kyoto to Edo, renamed Tokyo, meaning eastern capital. Why would rebels rule in the emperor's name rather than their own?

Watch the chain. Their slogan was rich country, strong army. The Iwakura Mission toured America and Europe from 1871 to 1873 to study railways, schools and armies. Lords' domains became prefectures, a national land tax paid for the state, and from 1873 peasants were conscripted. Which link took power away from the samurai?

stages.label: Central state
stages.note: Prefectures and a national land tax.

explain.say: Next came factories and schools. The Tomioka silk mill opened in 1872, the first railway ran from Tokyo to Yokohama, and an education order aimed at schooling for all. In 1877 Saigō Takamori led the Satsuma samurai in revolt, and the new conscript army crushed them. See the revolt light up. What did that victory prove?

explain.say: Strength turned outward: Japan beat China in 1895, Russia in 1905, and annexed Korea in 1910. See the two readings: a modernisation success, or an authoritarian state that taxed peasants hard and colonised its neighbours. Excellent work. Exam tip: compare Meiji Japan with Qing China's self-strengthening movement.

faq.a: The 1868 overthrow of the Tokugawa shogunate by samurai from Satsuma and Chōshū, who restored formal power to Emperor Meiji and then rebuilt Japan as a centralised, modern state.

faq.q: How did Japan modernise so fast?
faq.a: Leaders studied Western models through missions like the Iwakura Mission, abolished feudal domains, created a national land tax, a conscript army, railways, state-backed factories and mass schooling, all under the slogan rich country, strong army.

faq.q: Why did Japan build an empire?
faq.a: Leaders believed an empire was needed for security, resources and equal status with the Western powers. Japan took Taiwan after beating China in 1895, gained ground after beating Russia in 1905 and annexed Korea in 1910.
A rising in 1877 led by Saigō Takamori of samurai angry at losing their privileges. The government's new conscript army of commoners defeated it, ending samurai resistance.

faq.q: Why was the Russo-Japanese War important?
faq.a: In 1904 to 1905 Japan defeated Russia on land and at sea at Tsushima. It was the first modern victory of an Asian power over a European one, inspiring anti-colonial nationalists across Asia.

facts: Commodore Perry arrived in Edo Bay in July 1853.
Japan's first railway, between Tokyo and Yokohama, opened in 1872.
